pr_title: feat(medusa): Allow regexp in CORS configuration

comments.body: `parseCorsOrigins` splits on every comma before it tries to parse a regexp (`str.split(",")`). Any regexp that contains a comma gets cut into pieces. For example, `store_cors="/^https:\/\/a{1,3}\.example\.com$/"` becomes `/^https:\/\/a{1` and `3}\.example\.com$/`. The first piece doesn't parse as a regexp, so it falls back to a plain string. The second piece is also a string. The intended pattern never matches, and neither fragment is a valid origin, so requests from the intended origins are silently rejected. The same happens with `(a|b),c` style patterns. Use a splitter that respects regexp delimiters, or document that commas aren't supported.

The flag class `[gimsuy]*` accepts `g` and `y`. The `cors` middleware checks regexp origins with `regex.test(origin)`, and a global or sticky `RegExp` keeps `lastIndex` between calls. The same regexp object is reused for every request, so with `/.../g` the matches alternate. One request matches, the next fails, and so on. Valid origins then get intermittent CORS rejections. Either drop `g` and `y` from the accepted flags or strip them before building the `RegExp`. The test at build-regexp-if-valid.spec.ts:7 (`"/ab#/[c]/ig"`) shows `g` being accepted.
